7.0.s.en: (1) The lawfulness of both marriage and virginity

7.0.0.en: "Now concerning the things whereof ye wrote unto me", which is understood to mean that they were questions about marriage and not marrying: I would say to you that it is good for a man not to marry, if he is able, because virginity is a person's consecration of himself to the love of God.

7.1.0.en: If a man is unable to control his natural inclinations and to raise them to a higher level, let him marry, so that every man has his own wife only and every woman her own husband only.

7.1.1.en: It may seem from the above that marriage, as the Apostle indicates here, is merely a safeguard against falling into fornication, and that there is therefore something of a lowering of its dignity in this. But the matter is not so, because the Apostle himself spoke elsewhere of the lofty moral side of marriage and regarded it with honor and holiness (as in v. 14, ch. 11:3, Eph 5:25-27); the safeguard is one aspect of marriage in the view of St. Paul, and not all its aspects.

7.1.2.en: If you are married, do not forget that your goal, like that of the virgin, is the love of God. Give sufficient time every day to your prayers and your meditations on the Holy Bible. Moreover, use marriage as an opportunity to come out of your preoccupation with yourself and to offer love to the one with you, so that you rid yourself of the obstacles to the sense of God and always grow toward your goal.

7.2.0.en: The husband must feel the wife's due from him, which consists of tenderness and love; likewise the wife must render to the husband his due, which is esteem and faithfulness. This is recalled during the Prayer of the Crowning according to our beautiful Church rite, when the priest hands the bride to her bridegroom and says in the exhortation: You must, O blessed son, receive your wife in this blessed hour, and strive for what is for her good, and be tender toward her, and hasten to what pleases her heart. Likewise he says to the bride: And you, O blessed daughter... you must honor him and revere him and not go against his opinion... and meet him with cheerfulness and welcome, and not lose any of his rights over you, and fear God in all your affairs with him.

7.3.0.en: The husband and his wife become one flesh in the sacrament of marriage, so neither of them has power over his own body, but the other has it; therefore it is not the right of either to refuse the marital relationship because of lack of inclination for it, because his body belongs to the other. How then can he prevent the other from acting freely in what the other owns?

7.4.0.en: So I advise you that none of you withhold the marital relationship from the other, except with the consent of the other party to this abstaining, and for a certain period, so that they may devote themselves to fasting and prayer, and then the marital relationship is resumed, so that neither party is exposed to the temptation of Satan, who tries to make you fall into sin because of your inability to control your natural inclinations.

7.5.0.en: I say this meaning abstinence. It is necessary within marriage, as a declaration that the goal of marriage is love and the enjoyment of the presence of God between the spouses, and not a constant indulgence in bodily passions; so we enjoy this relationship but only for a time, and then return to our only goal in life, which is the love of God. And he says it by way of permission and not command, meaning that there is freedom in determining the periods of abstinence within marriage according to the need of each of the spouses and under the guidance of the father of confession.

7.5.1.en: There is another opinion, that his saying this refers to marriage as a whole, so it is by way of permission to whoever wishes and not a command, and whoever can live in virginity, that is better.

7.5.2.en: How beautiful is love within the sacrament of marriage, which makes each party forget his own desires and seek the comfort of the other, and this is so in all the matters of life. So care for the desires of those around you before your own desires, that you may rejoice in the smile on their faces and your heart be glad.

7.6.0.en: "For I would that all men were even as I myself", unmarried, that is, celibate; and yet I bear in mind that every person has his own abilities. One has a gift to live as I do without marriage, and another has the gift to marry.

7.7.0.en: I say to the unmarried, or those who were married but have become widowed, that it is good for them if they continue thus without marriage, as I live celibate.

7.8.0.en: Nevertheless, this approval of celibacy does not rise to the rank of a command; if these cannot control their natural inclinations while abstaining from marriage, let them marry, for it is better for a person to marry than to labor in resisting his natural inclinations.

7.8.1.en: If you are not able to attain complete bodily virginity, do not be troubled, but strive toward spiritual virginity, that is, that Christ be the Bridegroom of your soul, and that you take care to please Him in everything before pleasing yourself or others.

7.9.0.en: The phrase "I command, yet not I, but the Lord" does not mean that the previous opinions are personal opinions of the Apostle Paul, but means that what is to come was already spoken by the Lord in His Gospel (Mt 5:32). The Lord Jesus commanded that the woman not be separated from her husband, when He was on earth before His ascension into heaven, as recorded in the Gospels (Mk 10:9, Lk 16:18); that is, He commanded the stability of the marital relationship and forbade divorce except for fornication. So the people of Corinth, to whom the Apostle Paul writes, no longer needed teaching on this matter because they had the teachings of the Lord Christ.

7.10.0.en: If it happens that the wife departs from her husband for any other reason, let her remain thus without marrying another, and if she cannot live alone, let her seek reconciliation with him. And what I say of the wife I say of the husband also: he must not try to leave his wife. Thus in cases of marital disputes, reconciliation is the solution, and even in cases of fornication, if the other party forgives the party who committed fornication, they can be reconciled and live together. And from the teachings of the Lord Christ, to whom be glory, and the Apostle Paul's reminder of it, the Church does not allow divorce except on the ground of fornication. Our Church still holds to this law which the Lord of glory laid down to this day, and does not approve any divorce except for the ground mentioned.

7.10.1.en: When differences of opinion and problems occur between spouses, it is not right to quarrel or for either party to leave the house, lest the dispute increase and others intervene, and the distance grow and thoughts of separation and divorce by illegitimate ways begin. Let us give a chance to love, understanding and forbearance, and let each look to the virtues of the other and to the importance of preserving the structure of the family and not disturbing the children.

7.11.0.en: In the apostolic age, when a married pagan believed and his pagan wife did not believe, but she did not wish to leave her bond with her husband, let him keep her; and the reverse also: if the woman believed and her pagan husband was willing to remain with her, let her live with him in a normal married life.

7.12.0.en: The unbelieving party, when living with the other who believed, learns from him the Christian virtues, that is, is sanctified in him; and likewise the children learn from the Christian father or Christian mother spiritual conduct and become clean and pure.

7.13.0.en: "Under bondage": compelled to live with the pagan, because the pagan refuses to stay with the party who has become a Christian.

7.13.1.en: The believer may live with the unbeliever if the latter consents. But if the unbeliever wishes to separate from him, let the Christian party leave him, because he will not benefit from living with him, since the pagan is insistent on his conduct and his life, and there is no strong love binding him to the Christian party so that he would imitate his conduct and learn from him.

7.14.0.en: If it is possible for both parties, the believer and the unbeliever, to live in peace, the believer must not separate from the unbeliever, because in their life together there may be a favorable opportunity for the believer to save the unbeliever and draw him to the faith.

7.14.1.en: This permission which the Apostle Paul gave to the believers at the beginning of the spread of the faith was granted in special circumstances that existed then, but it is not for application at the present time, after the spread of the faith; the Church does not allow the marriage of a believer to an unbeliever, in accordance with the saying of the Scripture: "Be ye not unequally yoked together with unbelievers" (2 Cor 6:14). And this shows us the depth of the marriage bond.

7.14.2.en: The bond between the members of one family makes them influenced by one another's conduct. So pay attention to your behavior and your words, carrying out the commandments of Christ, so that you save your soul and be an example to those with you; and even if they oppose you or mock you at times, be confident that your good conduct has an effect on them. Do not be negligent or despair, and pray for them.

7.15.0.en: The Apostle makes clear the unimportance of the first condition in which a person was before the faith. Whether he was a circumcised Jew or an uncircumcised Gentile, what matters is that he walk as a Christian after his faith, and not try to change his bodily state by having the Gentile circumcised, because the proof of faith is keeping the commandments of God, as the Council of Jerusalem declared that the Gentiles who believed in Christianity had no need of circumcision (Acts 15:1-19, Gal 5:2).

7.16.0.en: Likewise the social condition of the pagan before the faith does not matter. If he was a slave, he is not asked as a believer to leave his master, but if he can become free, let him seize this opportunity (at that time a slave could buy his freedom by doing extra work for which he received pay and placing it in the temple of one of the gods until a sum equal to the price of his freedom was gathered, and then his master went to the temple and received this sum from the hand of the priest, and the slave became free).

7.17.0.en: "Freeman": that is, free in the Lord.

7.17.1.en: He who was called to the faith while he was a slave has in truth become free with a spiritual freedom, and the person who is free in his social standing must realize that true freedom is in submission to Christ. For true freedom, in both cases, is not outward freedom, but the freedom of the spirit from sin and its submission to God in holy worship.

7.18.0.en: Whether you are slaves or free in your social standing, you are slaves of Christ who bought you and paid a costly price for you, His most holy blood; so in all your conditions, slaves or free, you belong to Christ, so do not submit to the conduct of the wicked and become enslaved to them by imitating their sins.

7.19.0.en: Let each one remain in the condition in which he was when he accepted the faith, but let him take care to be always near to God and to live in a way that pleases God. In general, Christianity's remedy for social problems goes to the depth of the problem and not to its outward symptoms.

7.19.1.en: Do not be troubled by any deficiencies or weaknesses in you, for God completes them and supports you, so that your spiritual life or your service is not hindered, for God is able to work with the little and the weak so that you thank Him and glorify His holy name.

7.20.0.en: "Now concerning virgins" who are not married, I have no direct commandment from the Lord. For the Lord Christ, when He spoke about marriage and divorce, did not go on to speak about virgins; but I give my opinion as one chosen by the Lord and entrusted with the teaching, and I write a holy book under the guidance of the Holy Spirit to carry out the task of teaching. For because of the troubles and afflictions to which we are exposed in our present time, it is good for a person, whether a man or a virgin, to remain thus without marriage.

7.21.0.en: If you are bound to a wife, do not seek to leave her; and if you have not yet married, or were previously married and then separated from her for valid reasons, such as your pagan wife's separating from you, do not marry.

7.22.0.en: If you cannot control yourself in not marrying, it is no fault of yours if you marry. So also for the virgin: she does not sin in anything if she marries, if remaining as she is, a virgin, is beyond her capacities. But in general what I advise you is out of compassion for you, for the troubles and hardships you may encounter in connection with the persecutions which the Christians were undergoing at that time, since the married will meet more affliction. So the talk is about the circumstances of persecution in the apostolic age and not about virginity in general.

7.23.0.en: I say this to you, brethren: the time we live on earth is very short compared with eternity. So I advise you not to be occupied more than is fitting with our passing life, but with our spiritual duties which qualify you for eternity, so that the marriage bond with its responsibilities may not occupy you so that you give it all your time and all your heart, and it distracts you from your spiritual duty.

7.24.0.en: Do not let the sorrows or joys of the world occupy you either, for worldly joy, however great or large, is temporary joy, and likewise the sorrows of the world will one day end. Also, the possessions of this world or the greatness of position and authority must not distract you from the goal of your striving and struggle, which is the enjoyment of the eternal glories.

7.25.0.en: Those who possess much of the goods of this world must not yield to its enticements nor surrender themselves to its passions and pleasures. For all the things of this world, its appearances and its glories, soon end and pass away, so they do not deserve that we cling to them at the expense of eternity, which must be cared for in the first place.

7.25.1.en: Remember every day that it may be the last day of your life, so that you repent and prepare for eternity and live with Christ through your ordinary life, that is, so that your aim in your home, your work and all your relationships is to know God and show Him to others.

7.26.0.en: I would have you not be absorbed in the many responsibilities of marriage, because the unmarried can devote all his concern to what pleases the Lord, since the demands of married life do not occupy him.

7.27.0.en: But the married man has less concern for God, because he is occupied with worldly concerns which consume a large part of his time in order to provide the family needs for living in this world, and which please his wife.

7.28.0.en: The difference between the married woman and the virgin is that the unmarried woman can give all her time and effort to what pleases the Lord, being consecrated to Him in body and spirit because she is not bound by responsibilities which marriage imposes on her. But the married woman's married life requires that she turn to caring for what pleases her husband in all that he needs of her.

7.29.1.en: What I say in praise of not marrying and in speaking of the virtues of virginity, I do not intend to burden you, nor to oblige you to remain unmarried, which may be beyond your strength. I prefer that we live a life far from worldly entanglements and material preoccupations that can distract you from your spiritual worship, whether you are married or unmarried.

7.29.2.en: Would that we care for the things above, not the things on earth, always seeking what suits our eternity.

7.30.s.en: (9) The opinion on marriage while enjoying the life of virginity

7.30.0.en: This discourse is addressed to some believers who marry on the condition of abstaining from sexual intercourse in order to enjoy the life of virginity. He says to them: if the man does not behave toward the one who lives with him as toward a virgin, but as toward his wife, that is, if he feels the necessity of living with her as husband because of their inability to control themselves, let him do so; he does not sin.

7.31.0.en: He who has resolved with certainty in his heart, without compulsion, and has power and authority over his own will, to keep virginity for his wife, does well.

7.32.0.en: The man who lives with his wife does well and does not sin in this. But the man who remains a virgin with his wife according to their common desire and without compulsion does better. Thus the Church teaches us in our spiritual striving that there is a good state, but there is a better state. So let whoever can receive the better receive it; but each according to the gift he has been given and the spiritual stature he has reached.

7.33.s.en: (10) The dissolution of the marriage bond by the death of one of the parties

7.33.0.en: The married woman is bound to her husband according to the law of Christ as long as her husband lives, but if her husband dies she is free to marry whom she will, provided that the husband is united with her in the faith, so that her marriage to him accords with the will of the Lord.

7.34.0.en: But in my opinion she will be happier if she remains without a second marriage. I do not speak from myself, for the Spirit of the Lord who dwells in me guides me and gives me what to say so that I do not err. He permits marriage after widowhood, but prefers not marrying after widowhood as a kind of chastity, for the first marriage is enough, and he lives the rest of his life occupied with God, abstaining from bodily relations and the concerns of marriage.

7.34.1.en: Everything in the world God created for you; use it with freedom, but do not forget your goal, which is the love of God, and as far as you can, be content with the least possible of worldly attachments in food, drink, clothing and marital relations, so that you may give more time to your life with God and your service to Him.
